title: What this means for energy traders — Monday, November 23, 2026

sections.overall: Geopolitics dominates the headlines, and no corporate trend has confirmed yet. The digest's trend table is empty, so the ideas below are candidates only. Diplomacy with Iran, Houthi claims against a Saudi refinery and Libyan pipeline closures pull in different directions on oil. Meanwhile, LNG contracting and carbon-market policy keep producing steady, company-driven news.
sections.CRUDE_OIL: WTI fell 4.5% on the day as Trump signaled more time for diplomacy with Iran, with the report also noting rising global supplies (Rigzone). The IEA's view that markets can "manage without" Hormuz flows, though slowly, is a supply-side counterpoint to the disruption stories (FT). Headlines of this kind are usually read as shifting the balance between risk premium and supply. Whether diplomacy holds is still unclear.
sections.NATURAL_GAS: U.S. storage ended the injection season at 3,810 Bcf, almost 2% above the five-year average (EIA). On the contracting side, Woodside–Trafigura and the upsized Venture Global–China Gas deal show buyers and traders still locking in long-dated supply (LNG Prime). The Argentina project, with Eni, YPF and XRG named, adds a new supply region (TASS). Weather and storage data are typically the near-term drivers, and the digest does not settle how much the European cold-snap reports matter.
sections.REFINED_PRODUCTS: The picture is mixed. Record diesel prices pushed UK inflation to 3.6% (CNBC), and the Houthi claim on Rabigh adds supply-risk headlines (CNBC). Yet CNBC says the refinery-stock boom is unwinding (CNBC). Crack-spread direction remains an open question.
sections.CARBON_CREDITS: The EU–UK ETS link, agreed in principle with a 2028 start, gives the market clarity on design and timing, while Carbon Pulse analysts attribute the lingering UKA discount to execution risk (Carbon Pulse). China's plan to join CORSIA for 2027-29 and the EDF Trading–Econetix supply deal point to growing attention on aviation-offset supply (Carbon Pulse, Carbon Herald). COP31 ended without a deal, leaving carbon removal a contested topic (Carbon Herald).
